verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。用丝弦的乐器。）　神啊，求你听我的呼求，侧耳听我的祷告！
verses.en: For the music director, to be played on a stringed instrument; written by David.O God, hear my cry for help.Pay attention to my prayer.
verses.commentary:
61:1 Two parallel IMPERATIVES OF REQUEST start this Psalm (cf. Ps. 86:6;
Isa. 28:23; 49:1; 51:4; Jer. 18:19; Dan. 9:19; Hosea 5:1).

- hear my cry – BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE

- give heed to my prayer – BDB 904, KB 1151, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

▣ "cry" "Cry" (BDB 943) can refer to shouts of joy or, as here, a
cry for help and protection (cf. Ps. 17:1; 88:2; 106:44; 119:169; 142:6).

verses.zh: 我心里发昏的时候，我要从地极求告你。求你领我到那比我更高的磐石！
verses.en: From the remotest place on earth[NOTE:1] I call out to you in my despair.[NOTE:2] Lead me[NOTE:3] up to a rocky summit where I can be safe.[NOTE:4]
notes: Psalm 61. The psalmist cries out for help and expresses his confidence that God will protect him.

Heb “from the end of the earth.” This may indicate (1) the psalmist is exiled in a distant land, or (2) it may be hyperbolic (the psalmist feels alienated from God’s presence, as if he were in a distant land).
The imperfect verbal form here expresses the psalmist’s wish or prayer.
verses.commentary:
61:2 In Ps. 61:2 the psalmist says, "From the end of the earth I call to You." This
sounds like a prayer of an exiled person but the rest of the Psalm does not support this. Therefore, it
must be imagery of a sense of alienation by the psalmist.

The word "earth" can, in this context, be understood as "land"
(i.e., Promised Land), see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND,
COUNTRY, EARTH. Words have meaning only in context!

The AB understands the phrase to refer to Sheol (p. 84). This is based on
Ugaritic parallels. If so, the psalmist faced death, not just discouragement.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL, I. B.

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, Peshitta, JPSOA
"Lead me to""

REB
"Set me on"

LXX
"on a rock. . ."

TEV
"take me to"

The MT has the VERB "lead" (BDB 634, KB 685, Hiphil IMPERFECT.

- You will lead me ‒ תנחני

- You will set me ‒ תנחני

Only the vowels are different. So, the question is, "What is the allusion to?"

- God Himself, #1

- God's stronghold, #2

The UBS Text Project, p. 279, gives option #1 an "A" rating.

▣ "the rock that is higher than I" The title, "rock" reflects two Hebrew
roots (BDB 849 and 700 I). The title first (BDB 849) appears in Deut. 32:4,15,18,30,31. Notice how
it is expressed.

- the Rock – Deut. 32:4,15,18,30,31

- the Rock of his salvation – Deut. 32:15; 2 Sam. 22:47; Ps. 89:26; 95:1

- the Rock who begot you – Deut. 32:18

- their Rock sold them – Deut. 32:30

- their rock is not like our Rock – Deut. 32:31

- there is no rock like our God – 1 Sam. 2:2

- YHWH is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer – Ps. 18:2; 31:3; 71:3; 94:22

- My God, my rock, in whom I take refuge – Ps. 18:2; 28:1; Isa. 17:10

- who is a rock, except our God – Ps. 18:31

- YHWH lives, and blessed be my rock – Ps. 18:46

- my rock and my redeemer – Ps. 19:14

- my rock (BDB 700 I) – Ps. 42:9

- my rock and there is no unrighteousness in Him – Ps. 92:15

- blessed be YHWH, my rock – Ps. 144:1

- YHWH an everlasting Rock – Isa. 26:4

- to the mountain of YHWH, to the Rock of Israel – Isa. 30:29

- is there any other Rock? – Isa. 44:8

BDB 700 I occurs only in Ps. 18:2; 42:9. It literally means "rocky crag," but
is a synonym of BDB 849 (both used in Ps. 18:2).

This imagery has several possible origins.

- the mountain roots or pillars connected to creation

- the site of YHWH's giving of the law to Israel (Exodus 19-20, Mt. Sinai)

- the temple on Mt. Moriah (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH)

- the strength and permanency of physical mountains

- mountains are the highest point, closest to heaven where God dwells

▣ "higher than I" This could mean several things.

- the rock that provides salvation and refuge that the psalmist cannot provide himself

- the rock he is unable to climb or possibly understand (i.e., God's permanency)

- the contrast between God's exalted place and the psalmist's place of discouragement
(i.e., when my heart is faint)

The LXX and Peshitta have, "You left me upon a rock."

verses.zh: 因为你作过我的避难所，作过我的坚固台，脱离仇敌。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] you are[NOTE:2] my shelter,a strong tower that protects me from the enemy.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “on to a rocky summit [that] is higher than I.”
verses.commentary:
61:3 Much of the imagery used to describe God has military connotations.

- a refuge linked to a shield in 2 Sam. 22:31; Ps. 18:30; Prov. 30:5

- a refuge linked to a stronghold in Ps. 59:16

- here a refuge linked to a "tower of strength" (cf. Prov. 18:10) in Ps. 62:7, "the
rock of my strength"

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE

verses.zh: 我要永远住在你的帐幕里！我要投靠在你翅膀下的隐密处！（细拉）
verses.en: I will be a permanent guest in your home;[NOTE:1] I will find shelter in the protection of your wings.[NOTE:2] (Selah)
notes: Heb “a strong tower from the face of an enemy.”

Heb “I will live as a resident foreigner in your tent permanently.” The cohortative is understood here as indicating resolve. Another option is to take it as expressing a request, “please let me live” (cf. NASB, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
61:4 Psalm 61:4 has two COHORTATIVE VERBS.

- let me dwell in Your tent – BDB 157, KB 184, Qal COHORTATIVE,
cf. Ps. 27:5; 31:20; 32:7

- let me take refuge in the shelter of Your wings – BDB 340, KB 337, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW
AS METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE)

As Ps. 61:3 has military imagery, 61:4 has imagery related to the temple or possibly
"rock" in Ps. 61:2. The imagery of Ps. 61:4a is also found in Ps. 23:6; 27:4.

The term "forever" is PLURAL, which accentuates the concept (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER
['olam]). I think in this OT Wisdom Literature context it denotes a happy, long life in
temple fellowship (i.e., tent) with YHWH (cf. Ps. 23:6).

▣ "in the shelter of Your wings"
This is female imagery of God as a protective mother bird (cf. Matt.
23:37; Luke 13:34). See notes at Ps. 17:8 and

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE.

▣ "Selah" See notes at Ps. 3:2 and Intro. to Psalms, VII.

verses.zh: 神啊，你原是听了我所许的愿；你将产业赐给敬畏你名的人。
verses.en: For you, O God, hear my vows;you grant me the reward that belongs to your loyal followers.[NOTE:1]
notes: I will find shelter in the protection of your wings. The metaphor compares God to a protective mother bird.
verses.commentary:
61:5-8 This strophe relates to the King as a representative of YHWH's covenant people.

- The King has made vows (i.e., faith promises) to YHWH. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

- YHWH has given him/Israel the land (i.e., inheritance, cf. Gen. 15:12-21) of Canaan to
those who fear Him. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

- YHWH will prolong the King's life (i.e., royal hyperboles).

- The King will sit enthroned before God forever (obviously "forever" is not eternal
but prolonged days). Be careful of reading NT developed theology back into Hebrew terms (royal
hyperbole). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

- YHWH appoints (BDB 584, KB 599, Piel IMPERATIVE, prayer request)

- "lovingkindness and truth" (personified agents, cf. Ps. 40:11; 57:3; 89:14

- "goodness and mercy" in Ps. 23:6

- "light" and "truth" in Ps. 43:3)

This same concept is stated in Prov. 20:28. To uphold the King is to uphold Israel.

61:5 The MT has "the inheritance" (BDB 440, KB 442, LXX, Peshitta), which refers to the land of
Canaan divided among the tribes in Joshua 12-19.

However, the JPSOA and REB suggest an emendation to "desire" (cf. Ps. 21:2).

- the inheritance of. . . ‒ ירשׁת

- the desire of. . . ‒ ארשׁת

(BDB 77, which JPSOA thinks is an alternate form of root #1)

The UBS Text Project, p. 280, gives option #1 an "A" rating.

▣ "those who fear Your name" The NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 531, has a good comment
about "those who fear Your name." They represent the faithful followers (cf. Ps. 15:4;
25:12,14; 103:11,13; 118:4). NIDOTTE adds a list of slightly different forms.

- those who fear You – Ps. 31:19

- those who fear Him – Ps. 34:7

- those who fear Your name – Ps. 61:5

- those who fear God – Ps. 66:16

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 你要加添王的寿数；他的年岁必存到世世。
verses.en: Give the king long life.Make his lifetime span several generations.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you grant the inheritance of those who fear your name.” “Inheritance” is normally used of land which is granted as an inheritance; here it refers metaphorically to the blessings granted God’s loyal followers. To “fear” God’s name means to have a healthy respect for his revealed reputation which in turn motivates one to obey God’s commands (see Ps 86:11).

verses.zh: 他必永远坐在　神面前；愿你预备慈爱和诚实保佑他！
verses.en: May he reign[NOTE:1] forever before God.Decree that your loyal love and faithfulness should protect him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “days upon days of the king add, his years like generation and generation.”sn It is not certain if the (royal) psalmist is referring to himself in the third person in this verse, or if an exile is praying on behalf of the king.
Heb “sit [enthroned].” The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive here, expressing the psalmist’s prayer.
verses.commentary:
61:7 "He will abide" The VERB (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal IMPERFECT,
cf. Ps. 23:6) is a statement, but it is surely possible that this IMPERFECT is used in a
JUSSIVE sense, meaning it is a prayer request (cf. JPSOA, NET).

verses.zh: 这样，我要歌颂你的名，直到永远，好天天还我所许的愿。
verses.en: Then I will sing praises to your name continually,[NOTE:1] as I fulfill[NOTE:2] my vows day after day.
notes: Heb “loyal love and faithfulness appoint, let them protect him.”
verses.commentary:
61:8 Because of God's goodness to the King and Israel, the King will sing praises (BDB 274,
KB 273, Piel COHORTATIVE) to Him.

Again the use of "forever" must be seen as imagery for a long, successful
reign. The King's faith promises ("vows") are honored, performed, and fulfilled in the temple.
This close is similar to Ps. 30:12, thereby denoting a set ritual (i.e., thank offering) or liturgy
(connected to offering, cf. Ps. 7:17).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Is this Psalm an individual lament or a royal lament?

- Explain the phrase "from the end of the earth." Was the writer in exile?

- Does Ps. 61:4 imply eternal life? (cf. Ps. 61:7) Is this a Messianic Psalm?

- Define "vow" as it is used in this Psalm. (cf. Ps. 61:5,8)

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is obviously a royal Psalm (cf. Ps. 61:6). How God deals with the King represents
how He deals with the nation (cf. Ps. 61:5).

- At first, Ps. 61:2 seems to imply exile but the rest of the Psalm does not support
this. Therefore, Ps. 61:2a must be imagery of the King's sense of spiritual alienation.

- This Psalm has several memorable images of God.

- the rock that is higher than I

- You have been a refuge for me

- You have been a tower of strength

- let me dwell in Your tent forever

- let me take refuge in the shelter of Your wings
